The '''2013–14 [[La Liga]]''' season (known as the ''Liga BBVA'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 83rd since its establishment. Matchdays were drawn on 9 July 2013. The season began on 17 August 2013 and concluded on 18 May 2014; all top-flight European leagues ended earlier than the previous season due to the upcoming [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]. [[Elche CF|Elche]], [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and [[UD Almería|Almería]] competed in La Liga this season after being promoted from the [[2012–13 Segunda División|second tier]].

[[Atlético Madrid]], [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] traded the lead several times throughout the season. Entering the final weekend of play, Atlético Madrid were three points ahead of 2013 champions Barcelona. However, with the two teams facing off, Barcelona could claim the title with a win. The game [[Barcelona 1–1 Atlético Madrid (May 2014)|ended in a draw]], giving the ''Colchoneros'' their first league title in eighteen years, and their tenth overall. It was the first time since the [[2003–04 La Liga|2003–04 season]] that a club other than Barcelona or Real Madrid, who finished second and third respectively, had won the title. [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], [[Real Valladolid|Valladolid]] and [[Real Betis]] finished in the bottom three and were relegated.

[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] won the [[La Liga Awards|La Liga Award for Best Player]] for the first time. As the top scorer with 31 goals, Ronaldo also won the [[Pichichi Trophy]], along with sharing the [[European Golden Shoe]]. [[Ángel Di María]] had the most assists, with 17. [[Thibaut Courtois]] won the [[Zamora Trophy]] for best goalkeeper.

==Teams==

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
A total of twenty teams contested the league, including seventeen sides from the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]] and three promoted from the [[2012–13 Segunda División]]. This included the top two ranked teams from the Segunda División, and the victorious team of the [[2013 Segunda División play-offs|play-offs]].

[[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] and [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] were relegated to the [[2013–14 Segunda División]] at the end of the previous season; Mallorca were relegated after sixteen years in [[La Liga]], the longest period in the club's history, Zaragoza returned to the Segunda División after a four-year tenure in La Liga, and Deportivo made an immediate return to the second tier after being promoted the previous year. All three teams were relegated on the final matchday.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mallorca, Deportivo de La Coruña y Zaragoza, pierden la categoría y descienden de la Liga BBVA|trans-title=Mallorca, Deportivo de La Coruña and Zaragoza, are relegated from Liga BBVA|url=https://www.lfp.es/Noticias2/DetalleNoticia2/tabid/444/article/4592/language/es-ES/Default.aspx|language=es|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional|LFP]]|date=2 June 2013|access-date=9 June 2013}}</ref>

The three relegated teams were replaced by three [[2012–13 Segunda División]] sides: [[Elche CF|Elche]] returned to the top level as Segunda División champions, after 24 years of absence and having spent the last fourteen consecutive seasons in the Segunda División.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pérez|first=Javier|title=Un líder absoluto y austero|trans-title=An absolute leader and austere|url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2013/05/18/actualidad/1368902119_242372.html|language=es|work=[[El País]]|date=18 May 2013|access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref> Second-placed [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] were also promoted to La Liga, making an immediate return to the top flight<ref>{{cite news|last=López|first=Víctor|title=El Villarreal es de Primera|trans-title=Villarreal is in the First division|language=es|work=[[Diario AS|As]]|date=8 June 2013|access-date=24 February 2026|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2013/06/08/mas_futbol/1370706510_996039.html}}</ref> after a win over [[UD Almería|Almería]] in a decisive match near the end of the season which would see the winners directly promoted to La Liga.<ref>{{cite news|title=La gran final por el ascenso|trans-title=The grand final for promotion|last=Artús|first=José Luis|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20130608/futbol/liga-segunda-division/ultima-jornada-liga-adelante-villarreal-almeria_54375457942.html|language=es|work=[[El Mundo Deportivo]]|date=8 June 2013|access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref> Almería themselves also eventually achieved promotion; the club returned to the Spanish top flight after spending two years in the Segunda by defeating [[Girona FC|Girona]] in the final of the promotion play-offs.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/reportajes/2013/06/ascenso_del_almeria/seccion_00.html|title=El Almería cierra su triángulo mágico|last=Ferrero|first=Txabi|language=es|work=Marca|date=22 June 2013|access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref>

This was the first season since the [[1988–89 La Liga|1988–89 campaign]] without any teams from the [[archipelago]]s of Spain (teams located on the [[Balearic Islands]] and [[Canary Islands]]) in the top flight, as Mallorca were relegated and [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] failed to return to La Liga after losing in the semi-finals of the promotion play-offs.

==Season summary==
{{See also|Barcelona 1–1 Atlético Madrid (May 2014)}}
The 2013–14 [[La Liga]] season was the 83rd since its establishment. Match days were drawn on 9 July 2013.<ref>{{cite news|title=Calendario Liga BBVA 2013/14|url=https://www.lfp.es/portals/0/intercambio/Calendario2013_14BBVA.pdf|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional|LFP]]|date=9 July 2013|access-date=9 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810205601/https://www.lfp.es/portals/0/intercambio/Calendario2013_14BBVA.pdf|archive-date=10 August 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The season began on 17 August 2013 and ended on 18 May 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lfp.es/Noticias2/DetalleNoticia2/tabid/444/Article/4688/language/es-ES/proyecto-de-calendario-para-la-temporada-201314.aspx|title=Proyecto de calendario para la temporada 2013/14|trans-title=Calendar proposal for 2013–14 season|language=es|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional|LFP]]|date=6 June 2013|access-date=9 June 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609041425/https://www.lfp.es/Noticias2/DetalleNoticia2/tabid/444/Article/4688/language/es-ES/proyecto-de-calendario-para-la-temporada-201314.aspx|archive-date=9 June 2013}}</ref>

For the first time since 1951 and just the third time in league history, the [[La Liga]] title came down to a head-to-head match on the final weekend of play. [[Atlético Madrid]] were three points ahead of 2013 champion [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], but had its final game on the road in [[Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Last day drama in Spain|publisher=ESPN|last=Yokhin|first=Michael|date=16 May 2014|url=https://www.espnfc.com/blog/_/name/laliga/id/1879?cc=5901|access-date=19 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520043638/https://www.espnfc.com/blog/_/name/laliga/id/1879?cc=5901|archive-date=20 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Barcelona took a 1–0 lead into the half and Atlético lost two starters to injury in the half.  A second half header, however, secured a 1–1 draw, earning the ''Colchoneros'' their first league title in 18 years, and their 10th overall. It was the first time since the [[2003–04 La Liga]] that a club other than Barcelona or Real Madrid, which finished tied for second, won the title. It was also the first time in the 67-year history of the [[Camp Nou]] stadium that a visiting team had clinched the title in the stadium.<ref name=keys/>

The emergence of [[Diego Costa]] and [[Koke (footballer, born 1992)|Koke]] was a large part of Atlético Madrid's success. Costa scored 36 goals on the season (27 in league play), including the winner in Atlético's first victory over Real Madrid since 1999. Koke had 18 assists on the year (13 in league play), to go with seven goals.<ref name=keys>{{cite news|title=The 10 key factors in Atletico's title glory|last=Walker|first=Joseph|date=19 May 2014|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espnfc.com/blog/_/name/laliga/id/1935?cc=5901|access-date=19 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520041210/https://www.espnfc.com/blog/_/name/laliga/id/1935?cc=5901|archive-date=20 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Earlier in the season, [[Lionel Messi]] scored a hat-trick as Barcelona ended a 31-match unbeaten streak for Real Madrid. The same day, Atlético beat Real Betis to claim the league lead. A loss against Levante and draw against Málaga left Atlético vulnerable heading into their final match.<ref name=keys/>

[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] won the league scoring title with 31 goals. Messi was second and Costa third.<ref name=topscorer /> [[Ángel Di María]] had most assists with 17.<ref name=topassists/> [[Thibaut Courtois]] won the [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] for best goalkeeper.<ref name=zamora/> Barcelona was the least penalised team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spanish La Liga Stats: Team Discipline – 2013–14|date=19 May 2014|publisher=ESPN|url=https://www.espnfc.com/stats/fairplay/_/league/ESP.1/spanish-primera-division?cc=5901|access-date=19 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520041740/https://www.espnfc.com/stats/fairplay/_/league/ESP.1/spanish-primera-division?cc=5901|archive-date=20 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
